goal: Make the existing KitCode Welcome setup window detect the host OS and render a native-adjacent theme for macOS, Windows, and Linux while preserving the current onboarding flow, IPC contracts, and persistence behavior.

in: Detect setup platform from Electron `process.platform`, mapping `darwin`, `win32`, and everything else to `linux`, and pass that value into the setup renderer.

Render one shared setup flow with three platform themes: macOS traffic-light chrome and system typography, Windows title-bar controls on the right with Segoe styling, and Linux GTK/Adwaita header-bar styling.
Keep the existing setup steps and behavior: auto-track YES/NO, cumulative native multi-folder picker, Mini/Pet companion choice, save, optional tracker start, companion launch, and close.
Preserve accessible radio-group semantics, keyboard navigation, recoverable save/retry states, pending-versus-persisted project rows, and stable `data-testid` selectors.
Use per-platform semantic design tokens via CSS variables instead of one universal terminal palette; keep KitCode red only as the primary call-to-action accent inside each native skin.
Adjust Electron window chrome options per platform where practical (`titleBarStyle` on macOS, framed or right-side controls on Windows, GTK-style header bar on Linux).
Update focused onboarding checks to assert platform detection, per-platform theme markers, and unchanged functional selectors.
out: No `postinstall` or package-install GUI side effects.
No OS-themed redesign of KitCode Terminal, Mini, Pet, dashboard, or web setup gateway.
No changes to reward thresholds, equals counting, source snapshot rules, tracker daemon contracts, or local state schema.
No system light/dark auto-switching in v1; each platform theme stays on a fixed dark palette.
No localization or copy translation beyond platform-appropriate tone and keyboard hints.

acceptance_criteria.summary: Setup resolves `darwin`, `win32`, or `linux`, exposes it through initial renderer state, and binds `data-platform` plus platform-specific semantic tokens in the generated HTML.
On macOS, setup uses traffic-light chrome, system sans-serif typography, softer panel spacing, and macOS-style radio controls instead of the universal terminal/Vim presentation.
On Windows, setup uses right-side window controls, Segoe typography, Windows-like button and focus treatment, and Windows-appropriate keyboard hints.
On Linux and other non-macOS/non-Windows hosts, setup uses a GTK/Adwaita header-bar layout, Cantarell typography, and GTK-style primary/secondary controls.

Auto-track choice, cumulative project picker, pending removal, preferences-only save, tracker failure retry, companion launch, and `onboarding.completed` persistence behave exactly as before the visual pivot.

Each platform theme defines the same semantic token names (`--bg`, `--panel`, `--line`, `--line-strong`, `--primary`, `--primary-strong`, `--text`, `--muted`) without hardcoding unrelated one-off colors in the renderer logic.

coverage_plan.summary: Assert platform themes, semantic tokens, accessible controls, keyboard handlers, and unchanged functional selectors for all three platforms.
Run the Linux-themed setup interaction flow through headless Chromium with a mock bridge.
Re-run project registration and retry coverage unchanged.

risks.summary: The prior implemented setup plan standardized on terminal/Vim chrome everywhere; this requirement deliberately replaces that universal skin.
risks.mitigation: Scope the pivot to setup only and update focused checks to assert platform themes instead of terminal-only markers.

risks.summary: Electron HTML/CSS cannot perfectly replicate system controls on every OS.
risks.mitigation: Target native-adjacent chrome, typography, spacing, and focus language; document manual desktop QA as follow-up.

risks.summary: Existing onboarding checks assert terminal copy such as `NORMAL` and `[x]` notation.
risks.mitigation: Move assertions to platform-aware selectors and per-platform theme markers while keeping `data-testid` functional coverage.

implementation_handoff.summary: Add a package-local platform theme module, pass detected platform from onboarding Electron into the renderer, and restyle setup with three dark native-adjacent skins without touching tracker or reward contracts.
design_system_refs: Create `packages/kitcode-cli/src/onboarding-platform.mjs` as the package-local source of truth for setup platform resolution, per-OS semantic tokens, chrome fragments, and keyboard-hint copy.
Reuse the existing setup DOM structure and `data-testid` selectors from `onboarding-window.mjs`; do not fork separate HTML apps per OS.
Keep KitCode red (`#fc0a0a`) only on the primary save action across themes; use platform-appropriate accent/focus colors elsewhere.
suggested_sequence: Change `renderOnboardingWindow(platform)` and onboarding Electron window creation to consume them.
Replace terminal `[x]` marks with CSS-driven platform radio styling while preserving radio-group JS behavior.
Update focused onboarding checks for all three rendered themes and rerun the existing interaction/project checks.

verification.browser_evidence: Headless Chromium executed the Linux-themed setup flow: restored persisted NO, handled Arrow focus plus Space/Enter exclusive selection, appended and deduplicated two picker passes, removed only the scoped pending project, submitted autoTrack=false and companionView=pet with only the new folder, exposed a recoverable tracker failure, retried with an empty folder list, completed successfully, and had no body overflow.
environment_notes: Native Electron harness `npm run verify:onboarding-native -w @onedigitas/kitcode` timed out in this runner; browser interaction coverage uses `check-onboarding-interaction-browser.mjs` with headless Chromium instead.
Per-OS visual fidelity on real macOS, Windows, and Linux desktops remains a manual smoke check.
